title: Fixed: recognitions booked against the spend ceiling at the per-image rate
body: dda8072; router.run() substituted estimatePendingUsd (the dearest PER-IMAGE rate) for every unreported cost, including per-token recognize - 111 recognitions exhausted the default $5/h window and refused every generation after them. Also stopped labelling table arithmetic as basis:'vendor'.

title: Fixed: Leonardo cleanup failure logged the raw ImagingError object
body: a5e5239; console.warn(msg, e) printed .detail - up to 600 chars of raw vendor body, which can echo the user's prompt. Now log.ts logCleanupFailure(): one scrubbed bounded line that keeps the remote id.

title: Fixed: an unknown Leonardo cost unit was silently read as credits
body: 3106d2c; unit === 'DOLLARS' ? amount : amount * USD_PER_CREDIT divided any other spelling (e.g. 'USD') by 389 - the exact 400x error its own docstring warns about. Unknown units and non-positive amounts are now unpriced.

title: Fixed: pre-dispatch vendor limits raised bad-response, so they were billed and returned 502
body: 7342f70; Leonardo's 1500-char prompt limit and Qwen's 10MB inline limit are checked before dispatch, but billedOnFailure books bad-response unconditionally. New 'invalid-request' kind: 400, not billed, not reroutable; the budget probe pins it.

title: A single failed candidate discards the whole paid batch
body: google.ts runImage fires N concurrent calls and awaits Promise.all, so a 429/timeout/refusal on ONE candidate throws away the N-1 images the vendor already billed for; a 'refused' then reroutes the WHOLE batch to Leonardo and bills a second time. leonardo.ts has the same shape on the image downloads, and there the finally-block deletes the remote generation, so the paid images are unrecoverable. Recommendation: allSettled and return the images that did arrive, raising only when none did - but that changes what 'a batch succeeded' means, so it needs an owner's decision.
evidence: lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:291 (Promise.all over N paid calls); lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:150

title: The reroute chain's worst case outlasts the route's own maxDuration, and cleanup never runs
body: generate can spend 180s on Google (runImage timeoutMs 180_000) and then reroute to Leonardo, whose poll ceiling is MAX_POLLS*POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 180s. Worst case 360s against maxDuration = 300 on the generate route, so the platform kills the handler mid-poll: the caller gets a generic failure and leonardo.ts's finally-block - the cleanup contract its header calls load-bearing - never runs, leaving the generation in the user's gallery forever. Recommendation: give run() a request deadline it passes down as a shrinking per-hop timeout, or cut the ceilings so the chain fits the route.
evidence: providers/google.ts:287 timeoutMs 180_000 + providers/leonardo.ts:37-38 (60x3000ms) vs app/api/imaging/generate/route.ts maxDuration 300

title: The spend ceiling is per-process, so autoscaling multiplies it by the instance count
body: budget.ts holds the ledger in a module-scoped array and says so ('good enough for a single-instance prototype'). This repo deploys to Google Cloud, where more than one instance is the default, so N instances means N x the configured ceiling with nothing reporting that it happened. The code-side fix is a shared store; the cheap mitigation is pinning max-instances, which lives outside this context. Worth a decision rather than a rewrite.
evidence: lib/imaging/budget.ts:120 (let ledger: SpendRow[] = []) and its own header note at :21-25

title: lib/imaging/budget.ts belongs to no context in context-map.json
body: The map's imaging-providers entry was written 2026-08-14 and lists 18 files; budget.ts landed 2026-08-24 (12e6fdd) and is in none of them. grep over context-map.json finds 'imaging/pricing' and no 'imaging/budget'. The consequence is that the one file deciding whether a call may spend money sits outside every context-scoped sweep, review and KPI scan. Recommendation: add lib/imaging/budget.ts to the imaging-providers file_paths. NOT MINE TO EDIT - context-map.json is outside this context's boundary.
evidence: context-map.json:195 lists lib/imaging/pricing.ts; no line mentions lib/imaging/budget.ts

title: google.ts captures its env at module scope, against env.ts's written lazy-read decision
body: env.ts:12-14 states the rule and its reason: keys are read lazily per call rather than captured at module load, because a handler that booted before .env.local was filled in would hold a stale absence for the life of the process. google.ts reads GOOGLE_IMAGE_MODEL, GOOGLE_VISION_MODEL and GOOGLE_IMAGE_SIZE as module constants, so the same failure applies to the model and size overrides. Recommendation: read them where they are used, as env.ts does. Small, but it is a stated convention with one silent exception.

title: Two adapters disagree about what an empty vendor answer means
body: google.ts raises 'refused' for an empty recognition, with the argument written out at :112-122 - an empty result is how a block presents, and refused reroutes where a false success hands the caller nothing. qwen.ts raises 'bad-response' for empty content on every SKU, which is neither retryable nor reroutable, so in dev (recognize chain qwen -> google) an all-empty Qwen never reaches Google. Same condition, opposite routing. Recommendation: pick one and record why; if Qwen's empty is also a block, it should be 'refused'.

title: Vendor content types are asserted onto ImageRef's mime union rather than checked
body: leonardo.ts:153 puts fetchImageBase64's content-type straight into ImageRef mime with a cast; an expired CDN URL answering 200 with an HTML error page would produce an ImageRef the type system swears is a PNG, and the browser renders data:text/html;base64,... as nothing with no error to say why. google.ts:296 has the same cast plus a dead fallback (its left operand is always a non-null string). The three-value list is also declared twice - api.ts:20 MIMES and the union in types.ts:46. Recommendation: one exported IMAGE_MIMES plus an asImageMime() narrowing in types.ts. Held back as churn: real but low-impact, and it touches four files.
evidence: lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:153; lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:296; duplicate list at lib/imaging/api.ts:20

title: The browser client cannot send seed, which the route and every adapter honour
body: app/api/imaging/generate/route.ts:67 reads body.seed, GenerateRequest carries it, and google.ts:286 has a considered seed+i offset so N candidates differ while a run stays reproducible. imagingClient.ts's generateImage body type omits it, so no surface can reach any of that. Verified no consumer wants one today (grep over app/ and lib/ finds only unrelated 'seeded' state and one UI string), which is why this is reported rather than fixed - adding it enables a feature rather than repairing a defect.

title: A Google edit is still booked at the 1K generate rate
body: Deliberately left by the recognize fix (dda8072). google.ts:194-200 pins no image_size on an edit - so the plate keeps its resolution - and pricing.ts therefore reports it unpriced; router.run() then books the dearest per-image rate against the window. Unlike recognize this is at least the right UNIT, so it reads as a conservative stand-in rather than a category error, but it is still a figure pricing.ts refused to quote (it will not carry a 1K rate across sizes) entering the ledger as spend. Worth an owner's call: book nothing and let counters.unpriced carry it, or keep the guess and label it.

reason: Money paths: partial-batch discard on any single failed candidate, and every remaining place the ledger books a figure pricing.ts refused to quote.

title: Parallel-session hazard: a committed hunk was reverted, then half-restored
body: ccc5ffc committed lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts from a stale shared index and reverted 3106d2c+7342f70; e239239 restored the file to its 3106d2c snapshot, silently dropping 7342f70. It compiled and every probe passed, because the abandoned throw was still a legal ImagingError with the wrong kind. Re-applied as 9bdb360. LESSON: after a commit in this checkout, `git show --name-status HEAD` is not enough - the file was in every list. Compare HEAD CONTENT against the intended change, and re-audit at session end, not just after the commit. Second lesson: the shared index held pre-commit content for six files at session end; `git add <your paths>` after committing clears the phantom revert without touching a sibling entry.

title: Fixed: a failed step read no longer overwrites the stored cut
body: b5379a9; loadStep flattened a failed IndexedDB read and a never-written key to the same undefined, so the step re-derived seeded frames and the 600ms debounced save wrote them over a cut worth several dollars of plates. Now reads through readStep, disarms the save, and says so.

title: Fixed: secondsOf defers to the one timecode parser
body: 796c3cd; 'tbd' folded to 0, '1:02:03' returned 62, '90' returned 5400 - all silent, all confident numbers. Delegates to atSeconds, Frame.atS is number|null, durationOf answers null and skips unplaceable frames when looking for the next boundary.

title: Fixed: a plate batch stops on a systemic failure
body: 9623abf; generatePlate now returns ready|refused|failed so 'render N missing plates' continues past a vendor refusal of one subject and ends on a dead key or exhausted quota instead of firing all sixteen calls into the same wall.

title: Fixed: an unplaceable middle beat no longer hands its predecessor the rest of the cut
body: 02a5c7e; shotsFromBeats took beats[i+1] as the boundary without asking whether it parsed, so one bad timecode gave the preceding beat the whole remainder and multiplied its shot count. Forward scan plus a fail-before/pass-after probe.

title: Fixed: two beats at one timecode stay two groups
body: 730425c; shots.ts says beatAt is a position and positions repeat, and then grouped on it - the second beat's label and basis vanished and ShotSheet handed React the same key twice. Boundary is now ordinal 1 plus beatId; rows key by shot id.

title: Fixed: a cancelled drag ends the drag
body: c2b9d37; both canvas drag sites tore down only on pointerup, so a pointercancel left the move listener attached and the layer resumed following an unpressed pointer. One guarded bindDrag owns both.

title: Fixed: the plate-word map is keyed by PlateState
body: 8bfd21b; PLATE_WORD was Record<string,...>, so a sixth plate state would compile and read undefined.cls at render time.

title: Fixed: interactive state is announced, not only coloured
body: 3f0381d; view switcher and layer-select got aria-pressed, both halves of an assembly row got aria-expanded, and the fact-binding combo box got a name - it announced with none.

title: Fixed: Shot.roleDeclared's doc said the opposite of what the code does
body: f577ef2; the field is Boolean(b.role) and its comment claimed the inverse. A reader trusting it would have inverted beat-roles-were-declared and reported every declared beat as unmeasured.

title: The review and the direction pass still key beats by a repeatable timecode
body: reviewShotList counts beats with new Set(shots.map(s=>s.beatAt)) and check 1 groups resets into a Map keyed by beatAt; sceneSpec.reviewSceneSpecs builds byAt from f.at and rejects a second scene for the same key. Two beats sharing a timecode therefore under-count in the report and make the direction pass reject the second beat's scene as a duplicate. shots.ts already names this as the reason a shot is not folded into Frame[]. The fix is a beat identity carried through Frame and Shot - a seam change, not a rename.

title: Both ledgers are CSS grids with no table semantics
body: The assembly ledger and the shot sheet render a header row and data rows as sibling divs with grid-template-columns. A screen reader gets an unlabelled stream of text with no column association, so holds, pace, size and the verdict column are unreadable in context. Converting to table / role=table with scope=col headers is mechanical but touches every row renderer in both files.

title: A proposed prompt can be read only through a native title tooltip
body: The shot sheet's prompt column truncates to one line and puts the whole prompt - up to the 1500-character vendor ceiling - in a title attribute. A native tooltip cannot be selected, cannot be copied, and disappears on the smallest pointer move, so the page's own deliverable (a shot list you can read the prompts off) is the one thing on it you cannot actually read. An expandable row or a copy affordance is the fix.

title: Canvas layers can be moved only with a pointer
body: ResizeHandle grew arrow-key operation because role=slider promised it, but the layers themselves are still pointer-only: startDrag is wired to onPointerDown and there is no focusable target, no arrow-key nudge and no way to select a layer on the canvas from the keyboard. The layer panel can already select, so the missing half is a keyboard move on the selected ref.

title: ShotSheet re-derives the whole sheet on every parent render
body: shotsFromRender, unplaceableBeats, promptsForShots and reviewShotList (13 checks) all run in the component body with no useMemo, so every FramesStep render - and ctl's identity changes on every useFrames state change - repeats the entire derivation and review. Milliseconds today at 12 shots, and it scales with the cut. Four useMemos keyed on render/block.

title: generatePlate is re-created on every frame edit and the batch holds a stale one
body: generatePlate's useCallback deps include the whole frames array, so it is a new function after every keystroke in a text field. renderMissing captures one instance for the length of a serial sixteen-plate run, so a subject the user edits mid-batch is not the subject that gets sent. Reading the frame through a ref would decouple it.

title: The generated plate is announced as nothing
body: The plate img carries an empty alt, which tells assistive tech the image is decorative. It is the frame's picture - the thing the step exists to produce - and Plate.subject is a written description of it that is already in hand. alt={frame.plate.subject} would say what was asked for; an empty alt says there is nothing there.

title: /api/frames accepts any truthy style
body: The route rejects a missing style with a written reason and then accepts a string, a number or an array, JSON.stringify-ing whatever arrived into THE LOCKED VISUAL STYLE. A malformed style block is a multi-minute local Claude run spent on a brief nobody can follow, and the 400 that should have caught it costs nothing. A shape check for technique/subject/palette/finish is the same guard the client already satisfies.

title: isAuthoredClip trusts a clip's motion to exist
body: withClips fills a MISSING clip, so isAuthoredClip's f.clip?.motion.trim() covers the absent-clip case - but a stored clip object with a status and no motion (any future shape change, or a hand-edited record) throws inside a render rather than reading as unauthored. f.clip?.motion?.trim() costs one character.

Raised to /50 informational and /55 controls. The placeholder was /25; NumberInput's unit span, the one piece of text that component exists to render, was /35.

title: Fixed: a Modal mounted already-open never took focus
body: b41193d; Modal returns null until its mounted flag flips, so a first render with open=true focused a panel that did not exist and the effect never ran again. mounted is now in both the guard and the deps; it also stops the scroll lock firing for an unrendered dialog.

title: Fixed: the focus trap guarded disabled buttons only
body: d4c4cb7; the selector was button:not([disabled]),input,select,textarea - a disabled control, or an input[type=hidden] which matches bare input and can never take focus, could be picked as first or last, and then first.focus() is a silent no-op and Tab leaves the dialog.

title: Fixed: the colour-literal inventory was wrong by seven
body: ac1ad4a; tokens.ts states an exhaustive list of surviving colour literals. app/global-error.tsx holds seven more, all correct - it replaces the root layout so GravitoneTokens never renders and a var(--gt-*) resolves to nothing. Added as exception 4, with the hand-maintained ACCENT.cyan coupling named.

title: No text-colour token, and 241 sub-AA text-white/NN sites outside this context
body: Measured on the app ink #080a10: white/25=2.2:1, /30=2.60:1, /35=3.17:1, /40=3.77:1 - all below the 4.5:1 of WCAG 1.4.3, and none of this text is large enough for the 3:1 exception (most is 10-12px). 241 such sites across the other eight contexts. The design system declares NO text-colour token they could have reached for instead: TEXT existed but had zero readers and went in 782c3f9. The real fix is a measured dim-text scale in tokens.ts adopted call site by call site, which is a cross-context migration and cannot be driven from one context's sweep. /45 is the boundary worth knowing: exactly 4.50:1 on ink, 4.45:1 on glass.

title: StudioFrame hides the module nav below md: with no alternative
body: The nav links sit in a `hidden ... md:flex` container, so below 768px /library has no route at all - the wordmark reaches only /projects. There is no hamburger, drawer or overflow menu. Not fixed here because the honest repair is a mobile nav affordance, which is new UI and out of an --optimize sweep; and the cheap version, dropping the breakpoint, overflows a 360px bar once the wordmark, two labels, the bell and the avatar are laid out. Worth an explicit decision, because Modal.tsx already commits this design system to phones (it becomes a bottom sheet under sm:).

title: The design system has no golden-path probe, so its central claim is unchecked
body: tests/golden-path/ holds 17 probes and not one covers components/ui/ - the single reference is announcement.probe.spec.ts importing troubleAnnouncement, a pure string helper. tokens.ts calls itself the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH and globals.css consumes roughly twenty --gt-* vars by name; nothing asserts the two agree. A probe that parses globals.css for var(--gt-*) and set-compares against CSS_TOKENS + SIGNAL_DEFAULTS would make that claim executable in BOTH directions - an undeclared var that is read, and a declared token nothing reads. Both drifts were found by hand in this sweep (HAIRLINE/TEXT, and the stale literal inventory), which is the argument for the probe. Not written here: node_modules is mid-rewrite in this checkout and playwright could not run, and an unrunnable test is worse than a named gap.
evidence: ls tests/golden-path/ (17 probes); grep -rl 'components/ui' tests/ => announcement.probe.spec.ts only

title: A JS-passed behavior:smooth escapes the reduced-motion contract
body: 0854fe9 closed the CSS half (html{scroll-behavior:auto} under prefers-reduced-motion), but CSS cannot reach an argument: a scroll call that passes behavior:'smooth' explicitly still animates for a user who asked for none. One site does. It wants a matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') guard, or to drop the argument and inherit the now-correct CSS. Foreign file - frames-step context, named rather than touched.

title: Both text-rendering properties are declared on the universal selector
body: '* { -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; }' - both properties INHERIT, so declaring them on body produces the same output from one matched element instead of every node, and optimizeLegibility on a universal selector is a documented style-recalc hazard (it forces kerning and ligature work per element). Not fixed: 'visually identical' is the entire premise of the change, and this session was explicitly told not to run the build or the visual gate, so the claim would ship unverified. One screenshot diff settles it.

title: global-error.tsx's accent is a hand-kept copy of ACCENT.cyan with no drift detector
body: app/global-error.tsx must NOT read tokens.ts - it replaces the root layout, so GravitoneTokens never renders and a var(--gt-*) resolves to nothing on the one screen that exists because the shell already failed. That is correct and is now documented as exception 4 in ac1ad4a. But its #67e8f9 and #080a10 are copies of ACCENT.cyan and INK, and changing either here will not change them there, silently. This is the cheapest assertion in the repo (two string equalities) and belongs in the same probe as the tokens/globals.css cross-check above. Foreign file - app-infrastructure context.

title: Sweep of studio-design-system
body: 22 lenses evaluated (optimize / resolve); 16 findings, 10 fixed across 11 commits, 6 proposed, 1 escalation. Gate honesty: tsc --noEmit was green before every commit; npm run lint:ratchet returned exit 2 COULD-NOT-RUN for the entire session (node_modules/.bin empty, @eslint packages missing, and the missing module name CHANGED between runs - something outside this session is rewriting node_modules), and the playwright integration gate was deliberately not run and is owed. One incident worth carrying forward: commit ccc5ffc reverted a sibling session's leonardo.ts because HEAD MOVED between `read-tree HEAD` and `git commit`, so the commit carried a pre-sibling tree with a post-sibling parent. Repaired in e239239. The guard that catches it is SET-EQUALITY on the staged file list plus a HEAD-stability recheck immediately before committing - a deletion count does not, and the extra path was printed and read past.

title: Fixed: the trailer checker passed a spine it never read
body: 276a486; checkLadder keyed its long-cut verdict on droppedParts alone and reported pass -- "the full spine" over an empty cut, and over a one-beat cut its own report found missing escalation, climax, peak, reset and title. Empty cut is now not-engaged; the long-cut pass speaks only about the declaration. Pinned by a fifth property in trailer-structure-honesty.probe.spec.ts.

title: Fixed: the graph rule was silent over an empty cut
body: d4e8ed8; checkGraph's trailing row was guarded on beats.length && movements.length, so a cut with neither produced no graph finding at all -- and an absent rule reads exactly like a rule that ran and found nothing. Now not-engaged, naming the counts and pointing at the spine rows.

title: Fixed: note ids collided after a note was removed
body: 349f782; addNote minted both the id and Note.at from notes.length, which rewinds on removal, so two notes on one track could share an id -- one X deleted both, and the pad drew two children under one React key. Monotonic ref counter, seeded past the stored notes on hydration, read outside the StrictMode-doubled updater.

title: Fixed: the preset listbox swallowed Enter for the whole page
body: 6c6870e; While open, the listbox bound keydown to document, so any Enter on the page was preventDefault-ed and spent on the active preset -- a keyboard user typing in the sibling free-text field got their custom note AND a preset they never chose. Keys scoped to the component subtree, list closes on focus-out, options out of the tab order, aria-activedescendant added.

title: Fixed: the sticky pad did not survive a tab switch
body: 871fba6; StickyNotebook was mounted inside each of the four tab branches, so changing tab unmounted NotesProvider and Pad: the composer open on a track closed and a collapsed pad sprang back open, on the exact Coverage-to-Spend motion the step is built around. Mounted once; the tabs swap inside it.

title: Fixed: a missing prompt file surfaced as "the model could not be reached"
body: d85f094; systemPrompt()'s readFile await sat ABOVE the handler's try, so an unreadable pipeline/RECALIBRATE-PROMPT.md threw out of the route entirely: Next answered a bare 500, the client's detail fallback blamed the engine that was never started, and a simulated candidate was staged under that reason. Named PromptUnavailable, prompt built inside the try, 500 carrying the path.

title: Fixed: the running order read a sentinel as a timecode
body: fa63599; MatrixTracks parsed Usage.beats[0] with a bare split/Number, so the simulated path's "new" sentinel became NaN. NaN is falsy, so those rows fell through to the id tiebreak while real rows compared by time -- not a total order -- and "new" was drawn in the slot where a timecode goes. The parser now refuses a mark that is not one; unplaced cards sort after every real position and say so.

title: Fixed: verdict marks were a glyph and a colour only
body: 8a1d3d9; All three verdict panels in a render column -- the computed gate, the craft checks, the constraint ledger -- rendered the verdict as a bare glyph. GatePanel had declared MARK.label for exactly this and never rendered it. Glyphs are aria-hidden with an sr-only word beside them.

title: Fixed: selected state was a colour nobody could hear
body: 9d7c470; The four-tab strip, the version switcher, the zero-row filter, the spend sort and the pad's collapse all carried state in a border colour or a triangle glyph, and the tab and version labels are proper nouns that say nothing about which is live. aria-pressed / aria-expanded; deliberately not role=tablist, which would promise arrow-key navigation these buttons do not implement.

title: more-focus means two different things in the mock and in the route
body: recalibrate() applies a more-focus note to EVERY render, creating the card from nothing wherever it was unused. The route's rendersInScope() implements the note's own hint -- more-focus reaches everything only when NO render carries the card -- and otherwise scopes to the renders that already touch it. So the simulated fallback funds a card in renders the model path would never have been shown. Pick one reading and put it in one function both paths call. Left unbuilt: it changes simulated output and nothing tests it.

title: Four timecode parsers and two formatters in one context, and they disagree
body: editPlan.toS reads garbage as 0 ((a||0)*60+(b||0)); impact.toS reads it as NaN; trailer/types.atSeconds refuses; MatrixTracks now refuses. mmss is written twice (renders.ts, editPlan.ts). The commit that unified the beat and shot lanes (8165347) left the explainer lane untouched. One parser that refuses and one formatter, both exported from the step.

title: The gate is computed twice over the same chains, and one is the second answer the code warns about
body: ScriptStep memoises gateChains(chains) and threads it to the pad, with a comment saying a second gateChains call beside the button would be a second answer waiting to disagree with this one. GatePanel IS that second call: it runs runGate again per render over the same beats with the same options. Thread gate.byRender[renderId] down instead. Left unbuilt: three files of prop threading over working code, no user-visible gain beyond the invariant.

title: No structural rule reads TrailerBeat.at
body: atSeconds() exists, ShotLaneBeat.atS carries null for an unparseable mark, and the frames lane reports beats without a timecode -- but none of the trailer checker's 11 rules looks at `at` at all, so a cut whose beats carry malformed or backwards timecodes is reported well-formed. The checker deliberately does not SORT by at (a declared order is the author's), which is right; noticing that a position is not a position is a different rule.
evidence: app/_phases/script/trailer/structure.ts:112-115 - chain() returns cut.beats untouched and no rule reads b.at except where()

title: atSeconds accepts out-of-range components, so a malformed timecode reads as a plausible number
body: atSeconds("0:75") is 75 and atSeconds("1:99") is 159. The doc says it returns null rather than guessing, and 60..99 in the seconds field is a guess -- the one malformed shape that produces a believable answer instead of a refusal. Not fixed here: the parser is a shared seam the frames lane consumes and pipeline/trailer-structure-regression.mts pins its contract.

title: A 200 the client cannot read is reported as a failed request
body: useVersions.run parses the route body and calls recalibrateFromPlan inside the same try, and the catch stages a simulated candidate under "The recalibration request failed. Nothing was changed." A malformed 200, or a plan shape recalibrateFromPlan chokes on, therefore reads as a network failure -- the engine ran, cost real money, and the receipt says it was never reached. Validate the response shape at the boundary and give it its own message.

title: "adopt this one" records nothing
body: The adopt button on every render column sets a local useState in ScriptStep that nothing else reads -- not persisted, not sent to the route, not read by Frames. Grep confirms `adopted` has no consumer outside ScriptStep and HypothesisColumn, where it only tints a border. It is the one decision this tab exists to support and it survives neither a tab switch nor a reload. Either persist it through stepStore and let Frames read it, or remove the affordance.

title: Duplicate droppedParts entries pass silently and are printed back as the pass
body: checkLadder over droppedParts ["introduction","introduction"] returns pass with the detail "Drops introduction, introduction -- a prefix of the drop order". checkGraph validates movement ids, ordinals and beat ids but not this list, so the one duplicate the ladder can carry is the one nothing checks. Verified by driving checkLadder directly.
evidence: app/_phases/script/trailer/structure.ts:884-904 - drops iterated as a list, never as a set

title: A beat-order inversion names the innocent beat
body: Move a peak to the front of the chain and checkSpine's only report is that the STAKES beat belongs to an earlier movement than the beat before it -- located on the beat that did not move. The break after the first inversion is deliberate and documented, but the finding points at the wrong half of the pair, and this file's own rule is that a finding you cannot locate is a rumour. Name both beats in the subject.

reason: Mock and model paths compute the same recalibration and disagree on more-focus scope; diff them rule by rule.
Timecode parsing, gate computation and beat-position validation are each duplicated or missing across the step's two lanes.
